description: ADVERSARIALLY-PHRASED signal pool — model-authored, deliberately messy input for measuring distribution shift. The 400 signals in persona-signals.json are clean, well-formed phrasings; this pool exists to stress the student with the way real people actually type into a box: typos, shorthand, run-ons with no punctuation, vagueness, odd specificity, self-contradiction, non-native phrasing, venting, and assumed context the model cannot see. These feed ONLY the test-adversarial split; the eval reports test and test-adversarial separately, and a gap between them is a finding about distribution shift, not a failure. This is not a human baseline and must not be described as one.
instructions: Entries in `signals` are plain strings (no dimension/polarity tags — deliberate conflict construction only applies to the authored pools). Every string must be unique and must not duplicate any `s` value in persona-signals.json; the generator enforces disjointness and refuses to run the test-adversarial split with fewer than 40 entries (it skips with a warning when the split was only implied by --split all). Keep additions in the same adversarial registers: 'cheap but like not grim cheap', 'idk somewhere warm???', 'wife hates flying dont make it long', 'we is 4 person, one baby, hotel must have the lift'.
